steps.say: A car drives a loop through Karlsruhe. Its IMU logs a hundred times a second. Noisy position fixes arrive once a second.
steps.caption: OXTS truth, 1 Hz fixes, the ESKF estimate

steps.say: For thirty seconds, the fixes stop. Every filter drifts about forty metres, and the good ones know it.

scenes.headline: How a Kalman filter knows how wrong it is
scenes.sub: KF, EKF, UKF, the error-state filter and FAST-LIO's iterated update
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rudolf. Four filters, one real drive, and a test that tells you which of them is lying.

scenes.title: The update, in one line
scenes.text: x = x̂ + K (z − H x̂),  K = P Hᵀ S⁻¹
scenes.say: Every Kalman filter runs the same update.

parts.note: the prediction, pushed through the motion model
the innovation: what the sensor saw that we didn't expect
parts.say: Take the innovation, the part of the measurement you did not expect.

parts.note: the gain: prior spread over innovation spread
parts.say: And move by the gain. It weighs how unsure the prediction is against how unsure the innovation is.

steps.say: Rotations break it. A quaternion lives on a sphere, and adding a correction walks it off.
The error-state filter keeps the error in the tangent line at its estimate, then wraps it back on.
steps.term: Error state: a small correction in the tangent space

steps.say: Here a heading is a point on a circle. The filter predicts one direction. The sensor says the body is seventy degrees further round.
The classic EKF adds its correction in a straight line. It leaves the circle, so the code divides by the length and lands short.
The error-state filter solves for an angle and wraps it along the circle. It stays a rotation by construction.
The iterated filter relinearises at its new guess and solves again. Five passes later it is almost at the truth.
That iterated update is the loop inside FAST-LIO. It runs on every LiDAR scan, until it converges.

scenes.title: Error after the first range update
scenes.say: On the real drive, with ranges to beacons and a start thirty metres off, one linear step leaves the EKF eighteen metres out. Iterating gets within about a metre.

scenes.title: Starve Q and the filter lies

steps.say: To check a filter, weigh its errors by its own covariance. That is NEES, and a consistent filter averages the number of states.
steps.term: NEES: error squared over claimed variance

steps.say: Cut the process noise a hundredfold and NEES jumps past one hundred sixty. The filter is almost twice as wrong, and sure of itself.

left.title: Filter: fold the past away
left.say: A filter folds the past into one Gaussian and forgets it.

right.title: Smoother: look back
right.say: Run it backwards too, the factor graph's trick, and the error more than halves. When the answer can wait, look back.

scenes.text: Keep rotations in an error state, iterate when the measurement bends, and log NIS from day one.
scenes.say: Keep rotations in an error state. Iterate when the measurement bends. And log the innovation test from day one.

recap: The gain weighs prediction against innovation
Error states keep rotations on the manifold
NEES and NIS tell you when it lies
scenes.say: The gain weighs two spreads, error states keep rotations honest, and the chi-square tests tell you when a filter lies.
